findings.title: JSON contract paths bypass literal-code redaction
findings.finding: Document JSON fences are passed directly from JSON.parse to document-json shapes, and selected .schema.json/document .json sources are passed directly to json-schema-data. Their arbitrary nested strings are serialized verbatim and generally marked STATIC. staticData string hashing is only on the TypeScript initializer path and is never applied here.
findings.impact: A valid JSON Schema default/const/example containing guest implementation source would be copied into the catalog. No external reference was inspected, so occurrence in the pinned reference is not claimed. This is a supported-input library gap against the metadata-only/no literal code acceptance condition.
findings.remediation: Use a schema-aware bounded contract-data projection for JSON documents and schemas. Retain approved structural/type vocabulary, but represent unclassified payload/code-bearing strings with UNKNOWN, reason, source provenance, hash and byte length. Keep entries and owners rather than removing requirements. Review the analogous raw table/graph/annotation string channels under the same policy.
findings.verification: NOT_RUN: negative cases for code strings in both a schema file and a documented JSON fence; assert no literal bytes, preserved source/entry/owner and visible UNKNOWN.

findings.title: Live exported validation checks self-declared hashes without rebinding sources to the pinned tree
findings.finding: validateCatalog(catalog,{root}) compares each source SHA-256 to live bytes, then calls inspectReference, which authenticates package.json but does not read the supplied catalog sources through its pin-checking read function. source.git_blob is not checked. The filesystem inventory only rejects new candidate paths, not modifications at tracked paths.
findings.impact: With unchanged HEAD/package.json, a modified tracked source plus correspondingly recomputed catalog/source hashes can satisfy the live validator despite disagreeing with the pinned blob. This affects the exported standalone validator. The normal collector authenticates candidate bytes correctly; comparing against a trusted, unchanged frozen digest also supplies a separate protection.
findings.remediation: Create one inspectReference context and validate every supplied source through ref.read(path); compare its authenticated SHA-256 and relevant blob metadata. Refuse sources outside the declared candidate set or define such sources explicitly. Recomputable catalog hashes should remain integrity checks, not substitute for pin authentication.
findings.verification: NOT_RUN: change a tracked candidate while leaving HEAD/package.json unchanged, recompute only self-declared digests, and require validateCatalog(...,{root}) to reject it against the pinned blob.

notes.title: Generated distribution exclusion has a narrow path rule but no authenticated generatedness in this packet
notes.detail: The literal subtree python/sdk-runtime/src/deepseek_harness_runtime/runtime/ is excluded unconditionally, including any tracked files there. The comment retains artifact closure under P100-052; generatedness/ignored status is asserted in a comment, not verified by the helper, and the specific exclusion is not emitted as a catalog limitation or UNKNOWN closure entry. The rule is syntactically bounded. Whether that subtree is actually generated/untracked at the intended pin, and whether another artifact owns the complete denominator, was NOT_RUN and cannot be inferred here. Prefer emitting the exact exclusion, reason and owner to make this bound visible to downstream consumers. This note does not allege real lost reference requirements or establish parity.
